summary: Demo capture keeps agent authority unchanged: operator-only dispatch on the feature branch, protected command, secretless read-only job, verified definition and commit
basis: Traced the request path in run.py and demo.py, the workflow template and ADR-0012 against docs/policies/security.md and the R2 boundaries in docs/policies/project/workflow.md. Only the trusted ballast run demo can dispatch, after the tamper and in-progress markers and the run lock; agents keep gh, .github and ballast.toml denied. The command comes only from the protected [demo] table and is validated. Dispatch uses the feature branch, after a blob-identity check of the workflow; the job checks GITHUB_SHA and HEAD, and Ballast links only a run whose head_sha is the requested commit. The template has workflow_dispatch only, contents: read, no secrets or environment, inputs only via env, SHA-pinned actions, persist-credentials false, no cache. gh output is parsed into fixed codes; the ledger event is runner-only and text-free; packet text is inert. Two residual points are low/info and open. docs/policies/project/security.md does not exist. Same-provider review; live GitHub cache-scope behavior is post-merge pilot evidence.

findings.label: implementation-bug
findings.reason: demo._Request.dispatch refuses a branch equal to the run's base, not the repository default branch that check_workflow already read. They differ only for a PR whose base is not the default branch, and the published branch is the runner's own feature branch, so this is defense in depth: compare against the fetched default branch as well.

findings.label: spec-ambiguity
findings.reason: The outcome steps run in the same job as PR-head code, which can write GITHUB_OUTPUT/GITHUB_ENV or leave a background process, so captured versus failed is reported by untrusted code. Acceptable because a video is never evidence or approval (FR-014); worth one sentence in the policy's Demo capture section.
